name: Duwet
confidence_why: Holzknecht 1989, the only linguist to have done fieldwork on Duwet, refers to unstressed syllables and stress-conditioned vowel reduction in her phonological sketch but states no placement rule, and Holzknecht 2001 says nothing about stress, so the record rests on a single first-hand source that nothing contradicts and leaves the placement undetermined.
catalog_citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham Languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. (PDF + scanned text from ANU Open Research, handle 1885/145647)
catalog_locator: section 4.2.11 'Duwet' (phonological sketch), printed pp.56-57 = p.64, note 11; and section 4.6.26 'PMK *e' (scanned text)
catalog_quote: 4.2.11 DUWET ... Notes: ... 11. In unstressed position, the last vowel of a two-, tbree- [sic scanned: three-] or four- vowel sequence becomes [d] [scanned for schwa], e.g. siand 'sun' becomes sidnd; fuefueiaI) 'in small pieces' becomes fue'fueid1). 12. /ea,ua,ueia,ei,au,uo/: Diphthongs, in fast speech, are frequently reduced to a single vowel. ... [4.6.26] In the Lower Markham languages, the reflex of PMK *e is e. Duwet, in some etyma, exhibits a diphthong as reflex of PMK *e, and this varies between ia (iə in unstressed syllables) ei, e and i.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation (note 11 of section 4.2.11, plus the 4.6.26 'iə in unstressed syllables' remark) is present verbatim, scanned artefacts included, in the extracted text we hold and ANU scanned layers of Holzknecht 1989 at the stated place (printed p.56-57 = p.64-65). (2) Deciding source: a short phoneme-inventory sketch inside a 1989 comparative-historical Pacific Linguistics monograph by the only linguist to have done fieldwork on Duwet; it presupposes stress but gives no placement rule, so 'undetermined' is the faithful coding. (3) Better sources: Glottolog has one further descriptive item (Holzknecht 2001, morphology); downloaded from ANU Open Research and read -- no stress statement. No phonology article, grammar, instrumental study or thesis on Duwet (~400 speakers) was found; archive listings (OLAC/PARADISEC/SIL-PNG) could not be rendered and web search was unavailable this

sources.quote: None. The chapter is on person/number marking (pronouns, suppletive verb roots, base-two numerals); the only 'stress' token is the verb 'Duwet stresses this feature'. It mentions 'very complex morphophonemic alternations' and prenasalised-stop alternations but says nothing about word stress.
sources.note: The only other Glottolog descriptive reference for Duwet; checked in case it carried an orthography/phonology preamble with a stress note. It does not (silent).
